sections.title: Getting started — Adding your first photos
Full-screen viewer — Looking at photos up close

first-launch.title: First launch
first-launch.caption: When you first open Photonarium, you see the Database screen in the default light theme. There are no folders or photos yet — this is where you tell Photonarium where your photos live. The Edit Settings button opens an in-app settings editor where you can tweak advanced settings like model selection, face detection thresholds, and thumbnail quality.

dark-theme.title: Switching to dark theme
dark-theme.caption: Click the sun/moon icon in the top-right corner to switch to the dark theme. Most of the screenshots in this tutorial use the dark theme.

adding-images.title: Adding images
adding-images.caption: Click Add Folder to open your system’s folder picker. Navigate to the folder that contains your photos and select it. Note: on some systems the folder picker may open ‘behind’ the browser window — check your taskbar if nothing seems to happen.

indexing.title: Indexing
indexing.caption: Once you’ve selected a folder, Photonarium starts scanning it for images. The status changes to Updating and shows how many files are left to index.

processing.title: Processing
processing.caption: After indexing, Photonarium generates thumbnails and computes embeddings for semantic search. This runs in the background — you can start browsing as soon as the first thumbnails appear.

the-gallery.title: The Gallery
the-gallery.caption: All your photos appear here as a grid of thumbnails. Scroll to browse, or use the toolbar to sort, search, and manage your collection.

gallery-toolbar.title: Toolbar
gallery-toolbar.caption:
The toolbar runs along the top of the screen. When you have an internet connection, buttons display polished icons (loaded once from Google Fonts). Offline, they show simpler symbols instead. Both work the same way.

selecting-a-photo.title: Selecting a photo
selecting-a-photo.caption: Click any thumbnail to select it. A border appears around the selected photo, and the info panel on the right shows its details.

the-info-panel.title: The info panel
the-info-panel.caption: The info panel sits to the right of the thumbnail grid. It shows the filename, dimensions, date, and file size. You can also add a description and a rating to help you find this photo later. Use the toggle at its edge to collapse or expand it — handy when you want more room for thumbnails.

adding-a-description.title: Adding a description
adding-a-description.caption: Type a description and press Enter to save it. Descriptions are searchable, so a few words now saves time later.

auto-captioning.title: Auto-captioning
auto-captioning.caption: If you don't feel like typing, click the sparkle button to generate an automatic caption. You can edit it afterwards if you like.

emojis.title: Emojis
emojis.caption: Click the emoji button next to the rating field to open the picker. Choose any emoji to rate your photo — stars, hearts, whatever might help you to find that image later.

ratings.title: Ratings
ratings.caption: These can be any text you like. Emoji work well — try stars for favourites or hearts for the ones you love.

multiple-selection.title: Multiple selection
multiple-selection.caption: Hold Shift and click to select a range. You can also Ctrl+click to pick individual photos, or drag a box around a group.

sort-direction-flip.title: Sort direction
sort-direction-flip.caption: By default, photos are sorted by date. Click the arrow button to flip the current sort order.

sort-direction-restore.title: Sort direction
sort-direction-restore.caption: Click again to go back to the original sort order. Use whichever direction suits what you’re looking for.

similarity-select.title: Similarity
similarity-select.caption: Select a single photo to use as the basis for similarity sorting. Then click to sort by similarity. The grid will be rearranged so photos that look the most like the selected image appear first.

similarity-result.title: Similarity
similarity-result.caption: Here is an example of the Gallery sorted by image similarity.

fullscreen-opening.title: Opening
fullscreen-opening.caption: Double-click any thumbnail to see it full-screen.

fullscreen-controls.title: Controls
fullscreen-controls.caption:
The full-screen toolbar appears at the top. Click the edges of the screen (or use arrow keys) to move between photos.

👤person_searchToggle face tagging

⟲rotate_leftRotate left
⟳rotate_rightRotate right

❯chevron_rightNext photo (or Right arrow key)

navigating.title: Navigating
navigating.caption: Use the left and right arrow keys to step through your photos. You can also click the arrow icons at the edges of the screen.

zooming-and-panning.title: Zooming and Panning
zooming-and-panning.caption: User the scroll wheel to zoom in and out, then click and drag to look around. Double-click to toggle between zoomed and normal view.

fullscreen-closing.title: Closing
fullscreen-closing.caption: Press the close icon or the Escape key to return to the Gallery.

search-opening.title: Opening
search-opening.caption: Click the Search button in the toolbar to build a filter for your photos.

search-by-description.title: Search by description
search-by-description.caption: Type what you’re looking for. This is a smart search — it understands meaning, not just keywords. The similarity slider controls how strict the matching is: slide right for results that closely match your query, or left for looser matches.

search-results.title: Search results
search-results.caption: Pressing Apply shows the results in the Gallery, in order of how strongly they match your search. The toolbar shows that a filter is active.

negative-terms.title: Negative terms
negative-terms.caption: Put a minus sign before a word to exclude it. Here we’re looking for trees and plants, without people.

negative-results.title: Results
negative-results.caption: The Gallery now preferentially shows nature photos with people excluded. Negative terms are a powerful way to narrow down your search.

date-ranges.title: Date ranges
date-ranges.caption: Narrow your results to a date range. Leave either date blank for an open-ended range.

combined-filters.title: Combined filters
combined-filters.caption: Filters stack up — here we have a description search and a date range working together. Click Apply to see only the photos that match everything.

clearing-the-filter.title: Clearing the filter
clearing-the-filter.caption: Click the Clear Filter toolbar button to remove all filters and see your full image library again.

groups-opening.title: Opening
groups-opening.caption: Click Groups in the toolbar. The slider selects what kind of grouping to view — from exact duplicates on the right, through increasingly loose similarity levels, to directory-based groups and your own custom albums on the left. Each stack is a group of photos, with the count showing how many are in each.

groups-toolbar.title: Toolbar
groups-toolbar.caption:
The Groups screen has its own toolbar. The slider selects the strictness level, and Min size filters out small groups.

strictness.title: Strictness
strictness.caption: Move the slider to change how strict the matching is. Identical finds exact copies, while Related casts a wider net for photos with related contents. Beyond that, Directories groups photos by their folder on disk, and Custom is for your own hand-curated albums.

directories.title: Directories
directories.caption: Move the slider one position from the left to see Directories. These groups mirror your folder structure — each one contains the photos from a single folder. Group names show the shortest unique path needed to tell folders apart.

opening-a-group.title: Opening a group
opening-a-group.caption: Double-click a stack to open that group in the Gallery, where you can compare the photos side by side. They’re automatically sorted by quality, with the best one pre-selected. Select any you don’t want and press Delete, or just move on to the next group.

pruning-button.title: Pruning duplicates
pruning-button.caption: Once you’ve found duplicates, you can clean them up in bulk. The prune button (highlighted) lets you automatically keep the best images and move the rest out of the way.

pruning-dialog.title: The prune dialog
pruning-dialog.caption: The prune dialog gives you control over how many images to keep in each group: just the best one, a fixed number, or a percentage. A summary shows exactly how many images will be affected. Don’t worry — nothing is permanently deleted. Pruned images are moved to a ‘trash’ folder, so you can always recover them.

moving-between-groups.title: Moving between groups
moving-between-groups.caption: Use the toolbar arrow buttons (or Alt+Left / Alt+Right) to move to the next or previous group without going back to the Groups screen.

custom-level.title: Custom level
custom-level.caption: Move the slider all the way to the left to reach the Custom level. Unlike the auto levels, Custom groups are albums that you create and name yourself. The same photo can belong to multiple groups.

creating-a-group.title: Creating a group
creating-a-group.caption: Click the New Group button in the toolbar and type a name. The group starts out empty — you’ll add photos to it next.

adding-photos-from-gallery.title: Adding photos from the Gallery
adding-photos-from-gallery.caption: Back in the Gallery, hover over any thumbnail to reveal a small purple badge. Click it to open the Group Picker, where you can add the photo to existing groups or create new ones. If you have multiple photos selected, they’ll all be added at once.

the-group-picker.title: The Group Picker
the-group-picker.caption: Clicking the badge opens the Group Picker. The left panel lists available groups; click one to add the photo (right panel shows current memberships). Photos can belong to multiple groups at once — just select as many as you like. Click Done to save or Cancel to discard.

managing-groups.title: Managing groups
managing-groups.caption: On the Custom level you can rename or delete groups using the toolbar buttons. When viewing a custom group in the Gallery, select photos and press Backspace to remove them from the group without deleting the photos themselves.

faces-opening.title: Opening
faces-opening.caption: Click the Faces button in the toolbar. This screen is where you name the people Photonarium has found in your photos.

faces-toolbar.title: Toolbar
faces-toolbar.caption:
The Faces toolbar has its own controls.
OfflineOnlineDescription
─removeSmaller face thumbnails
✚addLarger face thumbnails
❔helpShow only unknown faces
⊕center_focus_strongFocus on one person
🔓lock_openShow unlocked faces only (in person view)

unknown-faces.title: Unknown faces
unknown-faces.caption: When you first arrive here, you see any faces Photonarium has detected. None have names yet — that’s your job! Each face has a name field below it.

typing.title: Typing
typing.caption: Click on a face and type a name into the field below it.

naming.title: Naming
naming.caption: Press Enter to save. This creates your first person. A Known People section appears at the top of the screen.

autocomplete.title: Autocomplete
autocomplete.caption: As you name more faces, suggestions appear while you type. Pick a suggestion to assign this face to an existing person.

failed-face-detections.title: Failed face detections
failed-face-detections.caption: Sometimes Photonarium detects something that isn’t really a face. If you spot one, you can click it to select it.

selecting-multiple.title: Selecting multiple
selecting-multiple.caption: Right-click to add more items to your selection without losing what you’ve already picked. Here we’ve selected eight false detections.

removing.title: Removing
removing.caption: Hover over any selected card and click the red X. Because multiple cards are selected, Photonarium offers to remove them all at once.

the-ignore-control.title: The ignore control
the-ignore-control.caption: For faces of people you don’t want to name, select them and click the grey minus button. This moves them out of the way without deleting the detection.

ignoring.title: Ignoring
ignoring.caption: Click the grey minus to ignore the selected faces. You can always rename them later if needed.

ignored-group.title: Ignored group
ignored-group.caption: The ignored faces now belong to a special person in the Known People section. They’re out of the way but not deleted, so you can always find them again.

quick-match.title: Quick Match
quick-match.caption: Click the sparkle button over a face to see who this face might be. Photonarium shows the closest matches from your named people. With more people named, this becomes a fast way to identify faces — just click a match to assign.

naming-another-face.title: Naming another face
naming-another-face.caption: In this case, we didn’t find a quick match so let’s name this face ourselves.

more-people.title: More people
more-people.caption: Press Enter to save. Now we have two named people in our collection, plus a group for all of the 'ignored' faces.

drag-and-drop.title: Drag and drop
drag-and-drop.caption: You can also drag faces directly onto a person in the Known People section to assign a name to them, including into the Ignore group. This also works with multiple faces selected.

view-all.title: View all
view-all.caption: Double-click a person to see all the faces assigned to them in one place. Here you can select - star - a preferred photo (setting their avatar), and lock correct identifications, or remove any faces with the wrong name.

preferred-face.title: Preferred face
preferred-face.caption: Click the star on your favourite image of this person. This becomes their avatar throughout Photonarium.

locking-and-unlocking.title: Locking and unlocking faces
locking-and-unlocking.caption: Locked faces (green padlock) are ones you’ve confirmed. Photonarium uses these as reliable examples when trying to recognise this person in other photos. You cannot unlock the preferred face! Unlocked faces may be automatically re-assigned at any time if a better match is found

faces-exiting.title: Exiting
faces-exiting.caption: Click the ⊕ / center_focus_strong (Focus on one person) toolbar button, or press Escape, to return to the main Faces screen.

tagging-opening.title: Opening
tagging-opening.caption: Let’s find photos of someone we’ve named. Click Search in the toolbar.

people-picker.title: People picker
people-picker.caption: In the People section, click Select people to choose who you want to filter by.

people-picker-select.title: People picker
people-picker-select.caption: Select people by clicking them, or drag them between the lists. You can pick as many as you like.

applying-people-filter.title: Applying the people filter
applying-people-filter.caption: Click Done, then Apply to see the results. The Gallery now shows only photos that contain Alice.

tagging-fullscreen.title: Full-screen
tagging-fullscreen.caption: Double-click a photo to open it full-screen. We know this one has Alice in it because of our filter.

enabling-face-tagging.title: Enabling face tagging mode
enabling-face-tagging.caption: Click the face icon (top left) to turn on face tagging. Coloured boxes appear around detected faces. Green means the face is named, red means it’s unknown, grey means ignored, and orange appears when you’re actively typing a name. Hover over a face to see the name.

tagging-naming.title: Naming
tagging-naming.caption: Click any face to type or change its name, right on the photo. Autocomplete suggestions appear as you type, and you have access to the sparkle button to access the Quick Match for a face, even if it has already been named or ignored.

tagging-ignoring.title: Ignoring
tagging-ignoring.caption: Hover over a face to see the same controls as the Faces screen. Click the grey minus to ignore, or the red X to remove a false detection. A green X will unname the face.

sorting-by-people.title: Sorting by people
sorting-by-people.caption: This groups your photos by who’s in them. Photos of the same person appear together.

switching-themes.title: Switching themes
switching-themes.caption: Click the moon/sun icon to switch between light and dark themes.

larger-thumbnails.title: Larger thumbnails
larger-thumbnails.caption: Click the Larger thumbnails button to make the grid bigger. Each photo shows more detail.

smaller-thumbnails.title: Smaller thumbnails
smaller-thumbnails.caption: Click the Smaller thumbnails button to shrink them back down. You can see more photos at once this way.
